example: Invented full-participation arithmetic, not experimental results

captions.text: Two clients keep their data locally; the server coordinates one shared model.
Broadcast the same parameter to both clients: each starts at w = 1.
Use the model y = wx and mean squared error; take two local gradient steps.
First step: gradients -2 and -8 give different local updates.
Second step: both gradients are now -1.6. The endpoints are 1.36 and 1.96.
Clients send their final model parameters; their training examples stay local.
Full participation: one example at A, three at B. Their weights are 1/4 and 3/4.
The weighted mean is 1.81: three times closer to B than to A.
Broadcast w = 1.81. Repeat local training and aggregation until the chosen stopping rule.
Keeping data local is not a privacy guarantee: model updates can still reveal information.
